correctness.rationale: For a label j≥3, the depth-two indicator depends only on attachment choices through j, and the survival-as-leaf indicator only on later choices. The latter has mean (j−1)/(n−1). The covariance with an earlier root attachment is its Bernoulli variance divided by n−1; the attachment at j is incompatible with depth two and gives the negative term −H_{j−2}/[(j−1)(n−1)]; a later root attachment precludes that arrival choosing j and gives H_{j−2}/[(n−1)(i−1)(i−2)]. The latter terms telescope. Summing over j yields H_m−H_m^(2)−m²/(m+1)² for m=n−2. The forward difference is (m²+m−1)/[(m+1)(m+2)²]>0, with exact values −13/144 at n=5 and 71/3600 at n=6. Standard harmonic asymptotics give the stated constant and growth. The independent attachment-history replay (`python -B /workspace/branches/replay_records_1_3_4_5.py`, section 5) agrees at n=3,…,8, including −1/4 at n=3 and −7/36 at n=4; it is supplemental to the unrestricted proof.

The Resultary leaf result gives Cov(R_n,L_j)=(n−j)/(n−1)² for the terminal indicator of each label j and its survival mean (j−1)/(n−1). Eslava studies high-degree depths and their limits, not this finite mixed moment.
broader_coverage.reasoning: If C_j is the known covariance of level one and unmarked level two at time j, then Cov(R_j,I_j)=C_j−C_{j−1} since the root attachment at j is independent of the past level-two count. Independence of the pre- and post-birth choices gives Cov(R_n,I_j L_j)=E[L_j](C_j−C_{j−1})+E[I_j]Cov(R_n,L_j). Thus these published profiles together determine the depth-stratified terminal covariance without a new joint moment.

Conditioning on birth versus survival is valid for this tilted model because its parent choices remain independent.

value.rationale: The contrast between a bounded total-leaf covariance and logarithmic depth-two terminal covariance is a natural observation.
